# Actual preserved-Mac warehouse audit: market-label consistency repair gate (2026-10-29)

**Finding confirmed against actual user-provided local DuckDB readback**, supplied as a small ZIP generated by `scripts.audit_preserved_warehouse`. The original **5,192,560,640-byte** private database has not been moved, uploaded or modified.

## Confirmed stored dimension issue

Built `dim_airport` has **8,802 unique airport codes** and **10 records** where `city_market_id` and `city_market_name` do not belong to the same source market row in the archived lookup.

| Airport code | Built CityMarketID | Built city-market name | Name for that same market ID in lookup |
|---|---|---|---|
| BAT | 36388 | Barth, East Germany | Barretos, Brazil |
| BDN | 36389 | Badin, Pakistan | Badana, Saudi Arabia |
| BGN | 36406 | Bruggen, Germany | Bagabag, Philippines |
| ISL | 32395 | Isabel Pass, AK | Istanbul, Turkey |
| KMC | 36392 | King Khalid Military City, Saudi Arabia | McCord, AK |
| LAC | 36393 | Pulau Layang-Layang, Malaysia | Papua New Guinea, Papua New Guinea |
| LOM | 36436 | Lagos de Moreno, Mexico | Loeriesfontein, South Africa |
| NEU | 36396 | Sam Neua, Laos | Nellie Juan, AK |
| SAW | 33459 | Istanbul, Turkey | Marquette, MI |
| TIC | 36401 | Turiacu, Brazil | Tinak, Marshall Islands |

The cause in `warehouse/build_marts.py`: selecting `max(CITY_MARKET_ID)` and `any_value(DISPLAY_CITY_MARKET_NAME_FULL)` independently for reused airport codes. Those fields can come from **different source rows**. The proposed builder code now orders source rows by descending `CITY_MARKET_ID` (preserving the legacy numeric ID selection), then by ascending source display name and descending source AirportID, and selects both attributes from the **same row**.

The change fixes **ID/name row consistency**, **not historical AirportID correctness**: a code reused for a different airport may still choose the wrong geographic CityMarketID. It is therefore insufficient to declare issue #7 complete.

## Other Mac-readback evidence

- `fact_segment`: **13,630,379** rows; `fact_od_market`: **173,741,663** rows.
- `map_citymarket_cbsa`: **815** rows; **0** duplicate CityMarketID->CBSA keys.
- `dim_metro_us`: **935** rows; `dim_metro_ca`: **37** rows.
- `ambiguous_latest_airport_lookup`: **36** codes; **17** map to more than one CityMarketID, **19** have multiple AirportIDs but only one CityMarketID.
- `unmapped_us_airport_codes`: **1,040 dimension airports** with no mapped CBSA. The top 100 unmapped-destination traffic groups include US territories and historic/non-CBSA airports (e.g. GUM, STT, SPN, STX, ASE, PFN). This is a **coverage/classification question, not 1,040 known missing passengers**. Current top-100 lists cannot certify all rows or eligibility impact.
- The only internal T-100 year gap is **2020**, omitted intentionally by the frozen project; **not automatically a data-loss event**.
- SHA-256 of all three local Mac published screen CSVs matches independently archived WestJet/Alaska/Porter CSVs byte-for-byte. None of the 10 mislabeled codes is a direct destination airport in the **200** screens; **indirect network consumers and 463 replay rows are not certified**.

## Safe merge and adoption gates

This patch changes only *future builds* of `dim_airport`; it **does not rebuild** the actual Mac warehouse or change existing outputs. A production adopt/rebuild must use a separate candidate warehouse file, preserve original source snapshots, and check:
1. All 8,802 airport codes and numeric CityMarketIDs remain unchanged versus the preserved warehouse; only expected market names change.
2. The `airport_dim_market_label_mismatches` diagnostic becomes zero in the candidate while the original stays unchanged.
3. Identify consumers of `city_market_name` in every model, carrier map, data mart, report and dashboard; record any affected label changes.
4. Verify equality of **200** screening verdicts and metrics and **463** historical replay decisions, with full source-fixed reproducibility tests. If any changes appear, investigate, do not silently overwrite.
5. Keep [airport identity issue #7](https://github.com/yumorepos/network-lab/issues/7), [geography issue #14](https://github.com/yumorepos/network-lab/issues/14) and other source-vintage issues open until their own gates are satisfied.

Synthetic tests in `tests/test_dim_airport_paired_market.py` exercise the exact builder helper against actual DuckDB/Parquet fixtures, checking corresponding row selection, stable tie breaking and no code duplication.

**Current decision:** review branch only. Do not merge and use this change as production-valid until the numerical and historical consumer gates are assessed.
